title: Token-level provenance and billing traces for per-token cost attribution
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Add low-overhead, token-granular telemetry that ties per-token latency, compute tokens, and KV-cache provenance back to request and billing records. This will enable: (1) precise cost attribution per request and customer, (2) latency breakdowns across prefix vs generation tokens, (3) cache-hit/miss impact analysis, and (4) dashboards/alerts for token-level regressions. Implementation spans runtime tracing hooks, metrics and logs pipeline enrichment, aggregation rollups, and dashboard panels in the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a compact trace span for each significant token event (start-generate, token-emitted, kv-cache-lookup) with well-known tag set
Trace spans include low-cardinality tags: model, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, route, customer_id_hash, cache_result (hit/miss), token_role (prefix/generation/assistant) and stage
Metrics pipeline consumes token spans and produces: token_latency_histogram per model_variant, cache_hit_rate per route, per-request aggregated token_latency and token_count
Billing pipeline can consume aggregated token_count and cost_estimate tag per model_variant for accurate per-customer cost attribution within 5% of offline estimator
Console dashboard shows token latency P50/P90/P99 split across token roles and highlights top 10 routes with highest token-cost regressions
Sampling and storage controls in place to bound telemetry cost (default sample rate 1% for full token traces, 100% for aggregated rollups), documented in design doc
Rollout via canary (5% of requests on dedicated runtime) with automatic rollback on increased tail latency or excessive telemetry cost
tasks: Design trace schema and tag vocabulary (tracing hooks API) - PRD reference: docs/design/token-provenance.md
Implement runtime instrumentation: token span emitters and lightweight counter hooks
Add KV cache provenance tagging (backend returns cache_result and provenance_id)
Enrich request context with customer_id_hash and route metadata before emitting telemetry
Pipeline: update collector to parse token spans and emit rollup metrics/logs to ClickHouse and metrics backend
Create aggregator job that computes per-request cost_estimate and writes to billing topic
Console: dashboard panels and alert rules for token-level regressions
Performance testing: simulate production traffic and measure telemetry overhead (target <3% p99 latency delta)
Run security review for customer_id hashing and PII risk
decisions: Use compact span format (binary/protobuf) for runtime -> collector to minimize overhead
Keep customer_id hashed at emit-time; do not emit raw IDs to telemetry backends
Store full token traces only under sampling; otherwise aggregate at source into per-request rollups
Cardinality control: seq_len_bucket and model_variant used instead of raw seq_len or exact model hash
Cost calculation will use model_variant unit price configured in billing service; telemetry emits token_count and token_role to allow weighting
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting held. Agreed tagging vocabulary and sampling defaults. Action: Jonah to author trace schema.

2026-03-01: KV cache provenance added; cache_result tag flows through pipeline. Observed cache-hit buckets align with experiment expectations.

2026-03-05: Security review kickoff completed. Requirement: salt + HMAC customer_id hashing; retention of full traces limited to 30 days for sampled traces. Action: Priya to complete threat model updates.

dependencies: PM-311 (pricing model updates for per-token unit costs)
risks: High telemetry ingestion costs if sampling/aggregation misconfigured
Potential PII leakage if customer IDs are not properly hashed before emission
Increased tail latency if instrumentation is synchronous; mitigation: use async emit and bounded buffers
Cardinality explosion if too many tag combinations are allowed; mitigation: enforce low-card tags and seq_len buckets
canary_plan: Stage 1: Internal traffic only (dev/staging) - validate metrics correctness
Stage 2: 5% production traffic routed to canary runtime with sampling defaults
Stage 3: Monitor 24h for latency regressions and telemetry cost; rollback automatically if p99 latency increases >5% or ingestion cost >2x estimated
Stage 4: Gradually increase to 25% then 100% with monitoring thresholds
notes: Prefer rollups that let billing reconcile with offline estimator for first 2 weeks before switching billing to live telemetry
Console panels should allow toggling between prefix and generation token views; helpful for prompt engineering troubleshooting
Coordinate with Customer Success for early customers that requested per-token billing visibility; opt-in flag required
